Kuvitus: keittiö iltaisin. Työtasolla ov: Illustration: a kitchen in the evening. On the worktop are a kettle with steam rising from it, a coffee maker, a toaster and a microwave oven, all plugged into wall sockets. On the left wall an open fuse board has a row of circuit breakers; one of them has tripped down. Through the window can be seen the evening sky and, far away, power line pylons.
Kytkentäkaavio, ei mittakaavassa: kodin: Circuit diagram, not to scale: one electrical circuit of a home. On the left is a 230 V alternating voltage source. The upper conductor runs from the source through a fuse to the right, and three devices are connected in parallel to it: two resistors with powers P1 and P2, and a lamp with power P3. The lower ends of the devices are connected to the lower conductor, which returns to the source. Purple arrows: the whole current I flows through the fuse, and it divides into the device currents I1, I2 and I3. Below is the equation I = I1 + I2 + I3.
Schematic picture, not to scale, two parts. On the left an earthed socket from the front: in a round recess are two holes for the line and neutral conductors and, at the top and bottom, metal protective earth contacts, labelled PE. On the right an electric cable with three insulated conductors coming out of its sheath: a brown line conductor L, a blue neutral conductor N and a yellow-green protective earth conductor PE.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa, kaksi panee: Schematic picture, not to scale, two panels. Each shows a device whose metal frame is drawn open: a brown line conductor comes from above to the resistor of the device, but its worn part touches the frame, marked with a spark and the word fault. A person stands on the ground and touches the frame of the device with a hand. On the left, without earthing, a purple dashed line and an arrow show the current I flowing from the frame through the person's hand and body to the feet and the ground. On the right, a yellow-green protective earth conductor is connected to the frame, and a purple arrow shows the fault current flowing along it; the text: the fuse trips. Only a small current flows through the person until the fuse cuts off the current.
Suojausluokkien merkit kolmessa sarakkee: Signs of the protection classes in three columns. On the left class I: the earth symbol, that is, a vertical line and three shortening horizontal lines, inside a circle; protective earthing, for example a washing machine. In the middle class II: two nested squares; double insulation, for example a hair dryer. On the right class III: a diamond with the Roman numeral three inside; protective extra-low voltage, for example a cordless drill.
Kytkentäkaavio, ei mittakaavassa. Vasemm: Circuit diagram, not to scale. On the left a 230 V alternating voltage source. The upper conductor is the line conductor L and the lower one the neutral conductor N. Both pass through a residual current device outlined with a dashed line, where they pass through the same iron ring. After that the line conductor has a fuse. On the right a device with a resistor inside its metal frame between the line and neutral conductors; between the line conductor and the frame there is a fault, marked with a spark. From the frame a current path leads through the resistance R body of a person to the ground. Purple arrows: in the line conductor the current I L to the device, in the neutral conductor the current I N back, and the fault current I f through the person to the ground. At the top right the equation I L minus I N is I f.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: maahan pudo: Schematic picture, not to scale: a fallen power line and step voltage. On the left a wooden pole whose broken conductor has fallen to the ground; there is a spark at the point of contact. In the ground around the point of contact are nested dashed arcs of equal potential; the colour fades from reddish to sand colour farther away, and an arrow tells that the potential decreases. In the middle a person takes a long step: their feet are on different arcs, and there is a step voltage U step between the feet. On the right a person stands with their feet together, and the voltage between their feet is almost zero.
Asteikko, ei lineaarinen: kehon läpi kul: Scale, not linear: the size of the 50 hertz alternating current I through the body in milliamperes on a logarithmic vertical axis from 0.1 mA to 1000 mA, each tenfold increase an equally long interval. Beside the axis a colour bar: below 0.5 mA green, 0.5-10 mA light orange, 10-50 mA orange and over 50 mA red. Labels: 0.5 mA the current can be felt, 10 mA the grip does not release, 30 mA breathing becomes difficult, 50 mA danger of ventricular fibrillation. Indicative values.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, laskettu malli: m: Graph to scale, a calculated model: the potential V of the ground in volts as a function of the distance r in metres from the point of contact of a conductor that has fallen to the ground, when the soil is uniform. The grid intervals are 1 m and 200 V. The curve falls steeply near the point of contact and levels off farther away; it passes through the grid intersections (1 m; 1200 V), (2 m; 600 V), (3 m; 400 V) and (6 m; 200 V) and through the point (4 m; 300 V).
Merkki: ympyrä, jonka sisällä on pystyvi: Sign: a circle with a vertical line inside it and three shortening horizontal lines at its lower end.
Merkki: vinoneliö, jonka sisällä on room: Sign: a diamond with the Roman numeral three inside.
